takeaway: A pretrained autoencoder (E, D) moves images into a low-dimensional latent space; the diffusion UNet εθ is trained and sampled only in that latent space, and conditioning y enters it through cross-attention via τθ.
problem: Diffusion models evaluate their network in pixel space at every step, which makes training and sampling at high resolution very expensive.

outputs: generated image decoded by D (x̃ during autoencoder training)

contributions.name: separation of the compressive from the generative learning phase
contributions.solves: costly pixel-space function evaluations: E/D are learned once, the DM never sees pixels
contributions.shown_by: out-and-back loop: E on the top row, D on the bottom row; the stage-1 path (x → E → z → D, dashed training-only) vs the stage-2 path; brackets name the two phases

contributions.name: Latent Diffusion Models (time-conditional UNet εθ in latent space)
contributions.solves: sampling is performed on a low-dimensional space
contributions.shown_by: the UNet is the only orange framed container, fed by green latent tensors (one latent tone everywhere)

contributions.name: cross-attention conditioning with the domain specific encoder τθ
contributions.solves: flexible conditioning on text, semantic maps or images
contributions.shown_by: conditioning column on the right (purple y → orange τθ) entering the cross-attention box inside the UNet with K,V

highlight: orange for the proposed UNet εθ and τθ (heavier framed container); green latent tensors; reused E/D in muted blue

mechanism.explains: cross-attention: Q from the UNet feature φ_i(z_t), K and V from τθ(y); its output goes back into the UNet layers (drawn in place inside the UNet container, not as a separate panel)
training objective: the UNet predicts the noise ε added to z_t, compared in L_LDM

concepts.name: out-and-back latent loop
concepts.takes: encoder on the top row running right, decoder on the bottom row running back left, photo thumbnails at both left ends; forward process on the top row, denoising on the bottom row; diffusion confined between E and D
concepts.sketch: row0: x → E → z ⇢(forward) z_t | y ; row1: x̃ ← D ← (z∼p(z)) UNet[conv φ_i ⇄ cross-attn] ← τθ ; row2: loss, ε → L_LDM

concepts.name: two stacked stage panels
concepts.takes: Step 1 autoencoder panel above, Step 2 latent diffusion panel below with the denoiser opened in place and the text branch entering from the lower left; latent drawn as a grid motif

concepts.name: one band per training stage
concepts.takes: full-width bands under dashed rules, the reused encoder/decoder redrawn in each band with the same fill, latents as 3-D cubes with sizes on arrows

why: At single-column width the loop keeps the figure to three short rows with E and D drawn once (c2/c3 must redraw or cross-link the decoder between panels); it shows at a glance that diffusion happens only in the latent space between E and D, which is the paper's point, and leaves the right column for the conditioning path into the cross-attention.
